skill.name: ddd-tactical-patterns
skill.description: Apply DDD tactical patterns in code using entities, value objects, aggregates, repositories, and domain events with explicit invariants.
skill.summary: Guide domain model design with DDD tactical patterns and explicit invariants.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Teams often scatter domain rules across controllers and services. This skill guides aggregate, value object, repository, and event design for clearer domain models.
actual_capabilities: Guides aggregate boundaries around transaction consistency.
Models immutable value objects with validation and value equality.
Defines repository contracts at aggregate root boundaries.
Uses domain events for meaningful state transitions.
limitations: Does not define strategic bounded contexts.
Does not choose databases or transport protocols.
Does not replace tests for domain invariants.
May add complexity when full DDD is not justified.

use_cases.title: Design an Aggregate Model
use_cases.description: Translate business rules into aggregate roots, invariants, and domain behaviors.

use_cases.title: Review Domain Boundaries
use_cases.description: Check whether repositories, value objects, and events respect tactical DDD boundaries.

use_cases.title: Refactor Anemic Domain Logic
use_cases.description: Move scattered service logic into behavior-rich domain objects with clear invariants.

prompt_templates.title: Find Domain Invariants
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a domain workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this domain requirement and list the invariants that should be enforced inside the domain model.

prompt_templates.title: Shape Aggregate Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for a transactional workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this workflow, propose aggregate roots, value objects, and rules that should stay inside each aggregate.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Domain Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these service responsibilities and suggest which behavior belongs in entities, value objects, aggregates, or domain events.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Tactical Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this tactical DDD design for aggregate leaks, weak invariants, repository boundary issues, and missing domain events.

output_examples.input: A checkout workflow allows empty orders and changes paid orders.
output_examples.output: The review highlights two invariants: submitted orders need at least one item, and paid orders should reject status changes.

output_examples.input: A customer profile uses strings for email, address, and phone values.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests value objects for validated contact details and explains where value equality should replace identity checks.

output_examples.input: A repository exposes ORM models and saves child entities directly.
output_examples.output: The review recommends repository methods that load and persist aggregate roots through domain-friendly operations.

best_practices: Start with invariants before choosing classes or tables.
Keep domain behavior inside entities, value objects, and aggregates.
Use domain events only for meaningful state transitions.
anti_patterns: Placing core domain rules only in controllers or application services.
Using aggregates as broad object graphs without transaction boundaries.
Letting persistence models leak into the domain layer.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design entities, value objects, aggregates, repositories, and domain events for domain-driven code.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it define strategic DDD boundaries?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on tactical implementation patterns after strategic boundaries are reasonably understood.

faq.question: Does it generate database schemas?
faq.answer: No. It can inform persistence boundaries, but it does not choose databases or schema designs.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when the task is only UI layout, API documentation, or simple CRUD without meaningful domain rules.

faq.question: How should I verify the resulting design?
faq.answer: Write tests for aggregate invariants, value object validation, repository contracts, and important domain events.
